l4_steps.name: Capture SSR from booking or service channel
l4_steps.input: Customer request via call centre, web booking, airport counter, or travel agent GDS
l4_steps.output: Raw SSR record attached to PNR
l4_steps.kpi: SSR capture rate ≥98% of requests received across all channels
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC channel requests may not automatically propagate IATA SSR codes into Altéa PSS, requiring manual re-entry and creating duplication risk

l4_steps.name: Classify SSR using IATA ADRM standard codes
l4_steps.input: Raw SSR record and IATA ADRM SSR code library
l4_steps.output: Standardised IATA SSR code assigned (e.g. WCHR, WCHS, WCHC, UMNR, MEDA, STCR, BLND, DEAF, BSCT, VGML, EXST)
l4_steps.kpi: SSR miscoding rate <0.5% of all SSRs entered
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents conflate WCHR (ramp wheelchair) with WCHC (cabin wheelchair), causing resource over/under-provision at the gate

l4_steps.name: Validate SSR code against passenger record
l4_steps.input: SSR code, PNR, flight itinerary, passenger age and loyalty tier
l4_steps.output: Validated SSR record or validation-fail alert
l4_steps.kpi: Validation completion within 4 hours of SSR capture for standard requests; <1 hour for MEDA cases
l4_steps.pain_point: UMNR age validation relies on data-entry accuracy — no automated DOB check against passport data until check-in APIS processing

l4_steps.name: Check aircraft equipment compatibility for SSR
l4_steps.input: Validated SSR code, assigned aircraft type, cabin configuration
l4_steps.output: Equipment compatibility decision (e.g. STCR requires aft bulkhead row; BSCT requires bassinet-mount rows)
l4_steps.kpi: Equipment conflict detection rate 100% prior to SSR confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute aircraft swaps (e.g. gauge change from 737-800 to 737-700) invalidate pre-assigned STCR/BSCT seats with no automated re-trigger of SSR review

l4_steps.name: Assess ground handling resource requirements
l4_steps.input: SSR code, flight schedule, station staffing roster
l4_steps.output: Resource allocation plan (wheelchair, ambulift, escort staff, medical oxygen)
l4_steps.kpi: Resource pre-positioning completed ≥2 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Third-party ground handler contracts at outstations often exclude specialised WCHC lift-on/lift-off equipment, requiring airline-owned asset repositioning at cost

l4_steps.name: Verify regulatory and safety compliance for SSR
l4_steps.input: SSR type, MEDA form, DOT 14 CFR Part 382 requirements, IATA Medical Manual
l4_steps.output: Compliance clearance or MEDA medical clearance request issued to CMO
l4_steps.kpi: MEDA clearance turnaround <6 hours for standard medical cases; 100% DOT Part 382 compliance audit pass rate
l4_steps.pain_point: MEDA cases require Chief Medical Officer sign-off but CMO availability outside business hours causes SSR holds and flight-day escalations

l4_steps.name: Confirm SSR and update PNR in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Feasibility approval, compliance clearance, resource plan
l4_steps.output: Confirmed SSR element in PNR with free-text OSI remarks for crew
l4_steps.kpi: PNR update latency <30 minutes from approval; SSR visible in all downstream systems within 1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: OSI remark field character limit (64 chars) forces abbreviation of complex medical notes, leading to misinterpretation by cabin crew at boarding

l4_steps.name: Broadcast SSR notification to all handling stations
l4_steps.input: Confirmed SSR elements from PNR, flight leg routing
l4_steps.output: Station-specific SSR notification delivered to each departure and transit station
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery confirmation rate ≥99.5%; transit station SSR awareness rate ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline/codeshare segments handled by operating carrier may not receive SSR notifications via SITA AMS if operating carrier uses a non-Altéa PSS — manual telex fallback required

l4_steps.name: Send SSR confirmation to passenger
l4_steps.input: Confirmed SSR details, contact preferences from loyalty profile
l4_steps.output: Confirmation email or SMS to passenger with SSR summary and pre-travel instructions
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger confirmation sent ≥24 hours before departure for pre-booked SSRs; <2 hours for same-day airport requests
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce CRM and Altéa PSS use separate customer identifiers — real-time SSR status sync requires middleware (API layer) that has a known 15-minute polling lag

l4_steps.name: Generate SSR pre-departure briefing sheet for crew
l4_steps.input: Confirmed SSR list for flight, crew assignment roster
l4_steps.output: Passenger Special Needs Brief (PSNB) attached to flight pack
l4_steps.kpi: PSNB delivery to crew ≥60 minutes before departure; crew acknowledgement rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late SSR additions (<2 hours before departure) do not always trigger PSNB update in Jeppesen — crew may operate on stale briefing data

l4_steps.name: Pre-position special equipment at departure gate
l4_steps.input: Resource allocation plan, SSR type, gate assignment
l4_steps.output: Equipment confirmed at gate (ambulift, wheelchair, STCR board, medical oxygen kit)
l4_steps.kpi: Equipment pre-positioned ≥45 minutes before boarding; zero gate-delay incidents attributable to missing SSR equipment
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambulift availability is shared across multiple gates at hub airports — competing WCHC requests on peak departure banks cause queuing and boarding delays

l4_steps.name: Review and protect SSR passenger seat assignment
l4_steps.input: SSR code, current seat map, aircraft equipment type
l4_steps.output: Protected seat assignment with SESL (Seat Especial Service Lock) flag; adjacent seats blocked where required
l4_steps.kpi: SSR seat protection applied ≥12 hours before departure; zero involuntary seat moves for SSR passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Upgrade clearance processes (Tier status upgrades) can inadvertently re-assign SSR-protected rows if the upgrade algorithm does not read SESL flags correctly

l4_steps.name: Verify SSR at check-in and issue special boarding pass
l4_steps.input: Passenger identity document, PNR with SSR elements, APIS data
l4_steps.output: Verified SSR, special boarding pass (e.g. pre-board marker), updated APIS manifest
l4_steps.kpi: SSR verification completion rate 100% at check-in; check-in processing time for WCHC/MEDA ≤8 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: APIS/ICTS name matching failures for passengers with SSR who also have name correction remarks cause check-in holds and require supervisor override

l4_steps.name: Coordinate pre-board assistance and boarding sequence
l4_steps.input: SSR passenger list, boarding gate assignments, special boarding pass flags
l4_steps.output: Pre-board completion confirmation; SSR passengers boarded and seated before general boarding
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-board completion ≥10 minutes before general boarding start; zero SSR passenger miss-boards
l4_steps.pain_point: Congested gate areas at hub turnaround stations make wheelchair manoeuvring hazardous; lack of dedicated SSR queuing lanes creates safety and delay incidents

l4_steps.name: Execute cabin crew SSR handoff at aircraft door
l4_steps.input: PSNB, boarding confirmation, SSR passenger seat locations
l4_steps.output: Cabin crew SSR acknowledgement; in-flight service adaptations confirmed (e.g. meal, oxygen, PA announcements for BLND/DEAF)
l4_steps.kpi: SSR handoff completed before aircraft door closure; cabin crew SSR briefing acknowledgement 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: High crew-to-SSR passenger ratios on wide-body or full narrow-body flights limit the attention available for complex MEDA or STCR cases during turbulence events

l4_steps.name: Record SSR fulfillment outcome post-arrival
l4_steps.role: Airport Customer Service Agent / Gate Agent
l4_steps.input: SSR completion status, any in-flight deviation notes from cabin crew
l4_steps.output: SSR fulfillment record with outcome code (Fulfilled / Partial / Failed) logged against PNR and customer profile
l4_steps.kpi: Post-flight SSR outcome recorded within 4 hours of block-in; SSR data completeness ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: No structured digital handoff mechanism between cabin crew and ground at arrival — fulfillment gaps are captured verbally or not at all, degrading SSR performance data quality

l4_steps.name: Trigger complaint or recovery action for failed SSR
l4_steps.input: SSR failure outcome record, passenger contact details, DOT Part 382 breach indicator
l4_steps.output: Proactive customer apology communication, compensation offer, and DOT incident report if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Proactive recovery contact within 24 hours of SSR failure; DOT Part 382 incidents reported within 10 days per regulatory requirement
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual identification of DOT-reportable SSR failures relies on agent judgement — no automated flag in Salesforce CRM triggers the mandatory DOT disability complaint reporting workflow

l4_steps.name: Analyse SSR performance and update service standards
l4_steps.input: SSR fulfillment records, DOT complaint data, NPS verbatims tagged to SSR journeys
l4_steps.output: Monthly SSR performance dashboard; process improvement recommendations; updated SSR handling SOPs
l4_steps.kpi: SSR on-time fulfillment rate ≥96%; SSR-related NPS ≥+45; DOT disability complaints per 10,000 enplanements <0.2
l4_steps.pain_point: SSR data is fragmented across Altéa PSS, Salesforce CRM, and SITA AMS with no unified SSR BI view — monthly reconciliation is manual and takes 3–4 days
